verdict.rationale: Jina Reader accepts natural-language input in two places: the `x-instruction` header steers ReaderLM-v2 extraction with plain-language instructions, and s.jina.ai takes free-form questions as search queries. An official MCP server also lets agents drive it conversationally. Overall operation, however, still runs through URL prefixes and many structured headers (engine, format, presets, token limits), so natural language covers only part of the control surface. Missing for 10: natural-language control of fetch and format options beyond extraction and search, hands-on corroboration of `x-instruction` quality, and detailed documentation of NL-driven workflows through the MCP server.
